IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p105/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p105/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p105/r7.claim: Those who are with their Lord are the angels.

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r1.claim: The surah is classified as late Makkan and reportedly followed Ṣād and preceded al-Anʿām.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r1.anchor:
A late Makkan sūrah, al-Aʿrāf was reportedly revealed afterṢād (
Sūrah 38) and just before al-Anʿām (
Sūrah 6).

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r3.claim: The surah warns of the grave consequences of rejecting God's signs and messengers, recalling prophets rejected by their peoples and the resulting suffering and destruction in this life and the next.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r3.anchor: the serious consequences of rejecting the signs and messengers of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.claim: The Prophet is urged to remain steadfast against opponents’ baseless objections and is shown what can help him persevere.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.anchor: At the end, the Prophet (sws) is urged to be steadfast in the wake of the nonsensical statements of his opponents and their baseless objections.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p160.claim: The last verse refers to angels, who never disdain worship and glorify and prostrate before God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p161.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p161.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p161.claim: People who continually remember and praise God on earth are spiritually joined to the angelic assembly, which likewise glorifies and praises Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p161.anchor: This is because just as the latter are constantly glorifying and praising God, these people too are doing so.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p161.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p161.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p161.claim: The verse rebukes idolaters who arrogantly expect angels to intercede for them while giving little importance to God and the Prophet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p161.anchor: they show arrogance because they think that they will receive intercession from angels

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p161.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p161.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p161.claim: The angels themselves continually glorify and prostrate before God, challenging the idolaters’ presumption about angelic intercession.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p161.anchor: such is the state of these angels that they are constantly glorifying and prostrating before God.

STUDYQURAN:7:206/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r1.claim: Those who are with the Lord are understood to be angels.
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r1.anchor: Those who are with thy Lord are understood to be the angels

STUDYQURAN:7:206/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r2.claim: The angels are with God in the sense of nearness to His Mercy and Bounty.
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r2.anchor: who are“with” Him in the sense of being near to His Mercy and Bounty

STUDYQURAN:7:206/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r3.claim: If pure and near angels do not disdain worship, imperfect and more distant humans have even less reason to refuse it.
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r3.anchor: if the angels, with their spiritual purity and nearness to God, are not too arrogant to worship Him

STUDYQURAN:7:206/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r4.claim: The verse echoes 4:172, where Jesus and the angels would not disdain being God's servants or worshippers.
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r4.anchor: where neither the messiah (Jesus) nor the angels would disdain to be a servant, or “worshipper,” of God

STUDYQURAN:7:206/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r5.claim: The angels' constant praise and glorification of God is mentioned elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r5.anchor: constant praise and glorification of God is mentioned in several places in the Quran

STUDYQURAN:7:206/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r6.claim: The angels' prostration is also mentioned at 16:49.
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r6.anchor: That they prostrate unto Him is also mentioned in 16:49

STUDYQURAN:7:206/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r7.claim: This is one of fifteen sajdah verses, marked in official Arabic Qurans to indicate physical prostration on recitation or hearing, though Islamic law does not require it.
STUDYQURAN:7:206/r7.anchor: Muslims should physically prostrate upon reciting them or hearing them recited although this is not required by Islamic law

TAB-FULL:v10p671/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p671/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p671/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī admonishes the listener not to disdain worship and identifies humble reverence as worship.
TAB-FULL:v10p671/r1.anchor: عن التواضع له والتخشع، وذلك هو العبادة

TAB-FULL:v10p671/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p671/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p671/r2.claim: The angels near God do not disdain submission and humble reverence to Him; this humility is worship.
TAB-FULL:v10p671/r2.anchor: عن التواضع له والتخشع، وذلك هو العبادة

TABATABAI:7:205-206/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r9.claim: The next verse explains the command: remember in this manner as those near God do, so as to join their company rather than leave it.
TABATABAI:7:205-206/r9.anchor: ظاهر السياق أنه في موضع التعليل للأمر الواقع في الآية السابقة فيكون المعنى اذكر ربك كذا وكذا فإن الذين عند ربك كذلك

TABATABAI:7:206/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:206/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:206/r1.claim: The phrase does not mean only angels, as many commentators explain; otherwise there would be no point in commanding people to remember as angels do.
TABATABAI:7:206/r1.anchor: إذ لا معنى لقولنا اذكر ربك كذا لأن الملائكة يذكرونه كذلك

TABATABAI:7:206/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:206/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:206/r2.claim: It refers generally to those brought near to God; nearness means presence without absence, and remembrance lifts the veil between God and the servant, since all things are otherwise equally related to Him.
TABATABAI:7:206/r2.anchor: بل مطلق المقربين عنده تعالى على ما يفيده لفظ { عند ربك } من الحضور من غير غيبة

TABATABAI:7:206/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:206/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:206/r3.claim: Lack of arrogance, glorification, and prostration characterize inward remembrance as well as spoken worship; they are not confined to bodily organs, as other verses show all creation glorifying and prostrating.
TABATABAI:7:206/r3.anchor: فيه أمور ثلاثة يتصف بها الذكر النفسي كما يتصف بها الذكر القولي

TABATABAI:7:206/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:206/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:206/r4.claim: The author contrasts this description with verses about those near God who glorify continuously without tiring; those verses imply uninterrupted remembrance beyond the intermittent discipline commanded here.
TABATABAI:7:206/r4.anchor: وما في الآية من توصيف القوم بعدم الاستكبار والتسبيح والسجود أخف وأهون مما يشتمل عليه قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:7:206/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:206/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:206/r5.claim: This verse calls for a degree of remembrance below the continuous, unbroken glorification described in the verses of al-Anbiyaʾ and Fussilat.
TABATABAI:7:206/r5.anchor: فهذه الآية تأمر بمرتبة من الذكر هي دون ما تتضمنه آيات سورتي الأنبياء وحم السجدة والله العالم

TABATABAI:7:199-206/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r15.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r15.claim: Umar reports that Gabriel warned the Prophet of posthumous communal discord: rulers would withhold rights, Quran readers would follow them into error, and restraint and patience would preserve people.
TABATABAI:7:199-206/r15.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور أخرج الحكيم الترمذي عن عمر بن الخطاب قال أتاني رسول الله

TABATABAI:7:206#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:206#2/r1.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:7:206#2/r1.claim: Al-Qummi identifies those near God in this verse as the prophets, messengers, and Imams.
TABATABAI:7:206#2/r1.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في معنى قوله { إن الذين عند ربك } الآية

TABRISI:7:205-206/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r10.speaker: الحسن وغيره
TABRISI:7:205-206/r10.claim: Those “at your Lord” are angels; despite their exalted standing, they worship and remember God, so humans should not be arrogant about worship.

TABRISI:7:205-206/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:205-206/r11.claim: “At your Lord” honors the angels through attribution to God; it does not mean spatial proximity, since God is transcendent above place.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r11.anchor: ولم يرد به قرب المكان تعالى الله عن ذلك وتقدس

TABRISI:7:205-206/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:205-206/r12.claim: An alternative explains the phrase as being in a place God has honored and under His sole rule, like soldiers said to be “at the prince” because they are under his authority.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r12.anchor: وقيل: معناه إنهم في المكان الذي شرفه الله تعالى ولا يملك عليهم الحكم إلا الله

TABRISI:7:205-206/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r13.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:7:205-206/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains being “at God” as being close to His grace and favor.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r13.anchor: وقال الزجاج: من قرب من رحمة الله وفضله فهو عند الله أي هو قريب من فضله وإحسانه

TABRISI:7:205-206/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:205-206/r14.claim: The angels glorify God by declaring Him free of what does not befit Him.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r14.anchor: أي ينزهونه عما لا يليق به

TABRISI:7:205-206/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:205-206/r15.claim: Sujūd may mean humility, prayer, or prostration in prayer; al-Hasan gives the last explanation.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r15.anchor: أي يخضعون. وقيل: يصلون. وقيل: يسجدون في الصلاة عن الحسن

TABRISI:7:205-206/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:205-206/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:205-206/r16.claim: There is consensus that this is a recitation prostration and the first such sajda in the Quran; Abu Hanifa deems recitation prostration obligatory, while al-Shafi'i and the author's companions call it a confirmed sunnah.
TABRISI:7:205-206/r16.anchor: ولا خلاف أن ههنا سجدة وهي أول سجدات القرآن واختلف في سجدة التلاوة هل هي واجبة فعند أبي حنيفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and other exegetes identify those with their Lord as angels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1) وغيره من المفسرين (¬2): (يعني: الملائكة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains being with God as nearness to His mercy and favor, not physical proximity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: (تأويله أنه من قرب من رحمة الله ومن فضله فهو عند الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r3.claim: Other people of meaning call this an honorific attribution: the angels are associated with God through their distinguished rank and the place from which His commands issue.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r3.anchor: وقال غيره من أهل المعاني: (هذا تشريف للملائكة بإضافتهم إلى الله عز وجل،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r4.claim: Another explanation says the angels are described as with God because they are His messengers to humanity, like an army said to be with a ruler though scattered across lands.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: (إنما قيل في صفة الملائكة {الذين عند ربك} لأنهم رسل الله إلى الإنس،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r5.claim: The mention of the angels' humility answers arrogant humans: even those greater than a human do not disdain worshipping God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p575/r5.anchor: جاء هذا على الجواب لمن استكبر من الناس عن عبادة الله، كأنه قيل: من هو أكبر منك أيها الإنسان

QASHANI:7:206/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:206/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:206/r1.claim: Those near their Lord are annihilated in divine unity, subsisting through God in steadfastness.
QASHANI:7:206/r1.anchor: بالتوحيد والفناء فيه باقين به ذوي الاستقامة

QASHANI:7:206/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:206/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:206/r2.claim: They are not arrogant because they are not veiled by ego; they witness differentiation within unity and submit to it.
QASHANI:7:206/r2.anchor: بسبب احتجابهم بالأنائية بل يشاهدون التفصيل في عين الجمع فيذعنون له

QASHANI:7:206/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:206/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:206/r3.claim: Their glorification denies association by negating selfhood.

QASHANI:7:206/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:206/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:206/r4.claim: Their prostration is complete annihilation, effacing all remainder and selfhood; God alone remains after creation perishes.
QASHANI:7:206/r4.anchor: بالفناء التام، وطمس البقية، وآثار الأينة، والله الباقي بعد فناء الخلق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r1.claim: Those near their Lord are the angels, close to God's mercy.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r1.anchor: يعني: الملائكة، وهم بالقرب من رحمة الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r2.claim: Despite their rank, the angels worship God; a being greater than a human does not disdain worshipping God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r2.anchor: أي: هم مع منزلتهم ودرجتهم يعبدون الله. كأنه قيل: من هو أكبر منك أيها الإنسان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:206/r3.claim: Their glorification means declaring God free of evil.

ELMALILI:7:206/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:206/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:206/r1.claim: Those near their Lord are the angels close to God, the high assembly, as described in Zumar 39:75.

ELMALILI:7:206/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:206/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:206/r2.claim: The angels do not disdain worship, glorify God, and prostrate only to Him; the Prophet is told to follow their example.

ELMALILI:7:206/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:206/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:206/r3.claim: Because of this meaning, prostration of recitation is prescribed when this verse is recited.
ELMALILI:7:206/r3.anchor: bu âyet kıraat edilince secde-i tilâvet meşrû kılınmıştır.

ELMALILI:7:206/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:206/r4.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm
ELMALILI:7:206/r4.claim: A Prophetic report says that when a person recites and prostrates at a prostration verse, Satan withdraws weeping: the person obeyed and earns Paradise, while Satan disobeyed and faces the Fire.
ELMALILI:7:206/r4.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm’dan öyle[^1] mervîdir ki Âdemoğlu secde âyetini

ELMALILI:7:206/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:206/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:206/r5.claim: Through remembrance, worship, and prostration, the way from the Heights to Paradise opens and its rewards are reached.
ELMALILI:7:206/r5.anchor: Demek ki bu zikr ü ibadet ve secde iledir ki a‘râftan cennete yol açılacak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r1.claim: Meccan polytheists were too proud to worship God by following Muhammad, especially through praising God and prostrating before Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r1.anchor: Mekke müşrikleri Hz. Muhammed’in dinine uyarak Allah’a kulluk etmeyi ve özellikle Allah’ı tesbih edip O’nun huzurunda secdeye kapanmayı nefislerine yediremezler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r2.speaker: müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r2.claim: Most exegetes understand “those who are with your Lord” to refer to angels.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r2.anchor: Müfessirler çoğunlukla “rabbinin katında bulunanlar” ifadesinde meleklerin kastedildiğini düşünürler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r3.claim: If even angels so near to God worship, praise, and prostrate, sinful human beings have even greater need for worship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r3.anchor: Allah’a yakınlıkları, “rabbinin katında bulunanlar” diye ifade edilecek kadar ileri derecede olan melekler bile kulluk etmekten geri durmayıp tesbih ve secde ederek kulluk faaliyetlerinde bulunduklarına göre her an günah işleme durumunda bulunan insanların ibadete daha çok ihtiyaçları bulunduğu açıktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r4.claim: Worship expresses a human station in which people move beyond animal limits and share a mode of action with angels.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r4.anchor: ibadetin, behîmî sınırları aşarak meleklerle ortak davranış düzeyine ulaşmış insanlara mahsus bir makamı ifade ettiğini göstermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r5.claim: Worship means recognizing God as Lord and expressing respect before Him through specified actions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r5.anchor: İbadet, kulun Allah’ı rab tanıyıp O’nun huzurunda belli davranışlarla saygısını ifade etmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r6.claim: Tasbih means declaring God free of every imperfection and exalting Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r6.anchor: tesbih, O’nu her türlü eksiklikten tenzih edip yüceltmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r7.claim: Prostration means lowering and placing the head on the ground only before God, after holding it upright before everyone else.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r7.anchor: secde ise herkese karşı dik tuttuğu başını sadece Allah’ın huzurunda eğmesi, yere koymasıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r8.claim: The sūra ends by urging people to honor worship, praise God with heart and tongue, prostrate humbly, prefer God's pleasure to desire, and share the angels' devotion rather than chase animal appetites.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:206/r8.anchor: Allah’a kulluğu en büyük şeref bilip dilimizle ve kalbimizle O’nu tesbih etmemizi, O’nun karşısında tam bir tevâzu ile secdeye kapanmamızı; Allah’ın rızâsını nefsimizin isteklerinden üstün bilip

BURHAN:v4p290/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p290/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p290/r1.claim: ʿInd and ladā basically denote nearness, which may be literal or figurative according to context.
BURHAN:v4p290/r1.anchor: وإذا ثبت إن عند ولدى للقرب فتارة يكون حقيقيا

BURHAN:v4p290/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p290/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p290/r2.claim: ʿInd may mean before or behind when context supplies the sense of before; waraʾ may likewise mean before or near, depending on relational context.
BURHAN:v4p290/r2.anchor: وقد تجىء بمعنى وراء وأمام إذا تضمنت معنى قبل

BURHAN:v4p290/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p290/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p290/r5.claim: Nearness to God can be figurative nearness of rank and favor; the angels described as near their Lord are the proximate angels.

ITQAN:v3p286/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p286/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p286/r7.claim: Other endings suit their suras: glorification in al-Ma'ida; promise and warning in al-An'am; worship urged through angels in al-A'raf; jihad and kinship in al-Anfal; praise of the Messenger in al-Tawba; consolation in Yunus and Hud; Qur'an's praise in Yusuf; warning and rebuttal in al-Ra'd.
ITQAN:v3p286/r7.anchor: وكالتبجيل والتعظيم الذي ختمت به المائدة وكالوعد والوعيد الذي ختمت به الأنعام وكالتحريض على العبادة بوصف حال الملائكة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p176#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p176#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p176#6/r1.claim: Those who are with the Lord are the angels.

NAHHAS:v2p173/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p173/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p173/r1.claim: The subject of inna is the angels.
NAHHAS:v2p173/r1.anchor: اسم إن وهم الملائكة صلوات الله عليهم

NAHHAS:v2p173/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p173/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p173/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq explains their being with God as nearness to His mercy; whatever is near His mercy is described as being with Him, while God is everywhere.
NAHHAS:v2p173/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق قال عند ربك والله جل وعز بكل مكان لأنهم قريبون من رحمة الله

NAHHAS:v2p173/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p173/r3.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v2p173/r3.claim: Another view places the angels where nothing is carried out except God's decree.
NAHHAS:v2p173/r3.anchor: وقال غيره لأنهم في موضع لا ينفذ فيه إلا حكم الله جل وعز

NAHHAS:v2p173/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p173/r4.speaker: قيل
NAHHAS:v2p173/r4.claim: A further view says they are God's messengers, as one speaks of an army being at the caliph's court.
NAHHAS:v2p173/r4.anchor: وقيل لأنهم رسل الله كما يقال عند الخليفة جيش كثير

NAHHAS:v2p173/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p173/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p173/r5.claim: They glorify God and declare Him free of every evil.
NAHHAS:v2p173/r5.anchor: ( ويسبحونه ) أي يعظمونه وينزهونه عن كل سوء

NAHHAS:v2p173/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p173/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p173/r6.claim: Their prostration means humbling themselves, unlike people of disobedience.
NAHHAS:v2p173/r6.anchor: ( وله يسجدون ) أي يذلون خلاف أهل المعاصي

ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r2.claim: Those who are with the Lord are the angels.

ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r3.claim: Their glorification declares God free of evil.
ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r3.anchor: يعنى به الملائكة. (ويسبحونه) ينزهونه عن السوء.

ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r4.claim: Although God is in the heavens and on earth, the angels are called near Him because they are near His mercy, favor, and beneficence.
ZAJJAJ:v2p398/r4.anchor: فتأويله إنه من قرب من رحمة الله ومن تفضله وإحسانه.

ASAD-NOTES:7:206#n168/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:206#n168/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:206#n168/r1.claim: “Those with your Sustainer” metaphorically describes utter God-consciousness.
ASAD-NOTES:7:206#n168/r1.anchor: a metaphorical description of utter God-consciousness

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#3/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#3/r2.claim: Al-A‘raf links the Adam story to its ending: the angels do not act arrogantly and do prostrate, unlike Iblis, whom the story portrays as arrogant and not among the prostrators.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12#3/r2.anchor: وقال في خاتمة السورة: {إِنَّ الذين عِندَ رَبِّكَ لاَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَيُسَبِّحُونَهُ وَلَهُ يَسْجُدُونَ}

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r17.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r17.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r17.claim: Tasbih, like istighfar, commonly uses the verb because it is renewed action; 7:206 and 62:1 illustrate this pattern.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3#2/r17.anchor: ومثل ذلك التسبيح فإنه ورد بالصيغة الفعلية كثيراً للسبب نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r13.claim: Those described as being with their Lord are the angels.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r13.anchor: إن الذين عند ربك لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ويسبحونه وله يسجدون هم الملائكة عليهم السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r14.claim: Their nearness to God is nearness in rank and standing, not physical location, reflected in their obedience and pursuit of His pleasure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r14.anchor: ومعنى العندية الزلفى والقرب منه تعالى بالمكانة لا بالمكان وذلك لتوفرهم على طاعته وابتغاء مرضاته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r15.claim: Lack of pride displays servitude and produces obedience; pride instead makes one imagine superiority and prevents obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r15.anchor: نفي الاستكبار عن عبادته وذلك هو إظهار العبودية ونفي الاستكبار هو الموجب للطاعات كما أن الاستكبار هو الموجب للعصيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r16.claim: Their glorification means declaring God transcendent and purifying Him of everything unfitting for His sacred essence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p263/r16.anchor: إثبات التسبيح منهم له تعالى وهو التنزيه والتطهير عن جميع ما لا يليق بذاته المقدسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r1.claim: A view takes the fronted object as restriction: the angels prostrate to Him alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r1.anchor: وتقديم المجرور يؤذن بالاختصاص أي لا يسجدون إلا له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān instead says the object is fronted to make the clause an appropriate verse ending matching the surrounding endings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r2.anchor: والذي يظهر أنه إنما قدم المجرور ليقع الفعل فاصلة فأخره لذلك ليناسب ما قبله من رؤوس الآي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r3.claim: Worship follows from freedom from pride and has inward and bodily forms: glorifying God and prostrating, when the servant is closest to Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r3.anchor: ولما كانت العبادة ناشئة عن انتفاء الاستكبار وكانت على قسمين عبادة قلبية وعبادة جسمانية ذكرهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r4.claim: He cites a hadith that the heavens creak, with no span except that an angel there is standing, bowing, or prostrating.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث «أطت السماء وحق لها أن تئط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r5.claim: The verse marks a place for prostration during Qurʾān recitation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r5.anchor: وله يسجدون هو مكان سجدة وقيل: سجود التلاوة أربع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r6.claim: One count recognizes four recitation prostrations: alif-lām-mīm tanzīl, ḥā-mīm tanzīl, al-Najm, and al-ʿAlaq.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r6.anchor: وقيل: سجود التلاوة أربع سجدات ألم تنزيل وحم تنزيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports ten recitation prostrations, omitting the last of al-Ḥajj, Ṣād, and the three in the short sūras.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r7.anchor: وذكر عن ابن عباس أنها عشر أسقط آخر الحج وص وثلاثا في المفصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r8.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r8.claim: Mālik's reported count is eleven, omitting the last prostration of al-Ḥajj and the three in the short sūras.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r8.anchor: وروي عن مالك إحدى عشرة أسقط آخرة الحج وثلاث المفصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r9.speaker: ابن وهب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r9.claim: Ibn Wahb reports fourteen prostrations, omitting the second prostration in al-Ḥajj.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r9.anchor: وعن ابن وهب أربع عشرة أسقط ثانية الحج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r10.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī count fourteen but differ over the locations: Abū Ḥanīfa omits the second of al-Ḥajj and includes Ṣād; al-Shāfiʿī reverses them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r10.anchor: وهو قول أبي حنيفة والشافعي لكن أبو حنيفة أسقط ثانية الحج وأثبت ص وعكس الشافعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r11.speaker: ابن وهب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r11.claim: Ibn Wahb and Ibn Ḥabīb also report a count of fifteen, ending with the final prostration of al-ʿAlaq.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r11.anchor: وعن ابن وهب أيضا وابن حبيب خمس عشرة آخرها خاتمة العلق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r12.claim: Some scholars count sixteen prostrations by adding the prostration in al-Ḥijr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r12.anchor: وعن بعض العلماء ست عشرة وزاد سجدة الحجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r13.claim: The majority hold that recitation prostration is not obligatory; Abū Ḥanīfa holds that it is obligatory.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r13.anchor: والجمهور على أنه ليس بواجب وقال أبو حنيفة هو واجب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r14.claim: Its conditions are those of prayer: purity from impurity and ritual defilement, intention, and facing the qibla; a report in al-Bukhārī permits prostration without purity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r14.anchor: ولا خلاف في أن شرطه شرط الصلاة من طهارة خبث وحدث ونية واستقبال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r15.speaker: ابن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r15.claim: Al-Bukhārī relates from Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn al-Munkadir from al-Shaʿbī that one may prostrate without ritual purity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r15.anchor: إلا ما روى البخاري عن ابن عمر وابن المنكدر عن الشعبي أنه يسجد على غير طهارة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r16.speaker: الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r16.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and Isḥāq say to say the takbīr and raise the hands for the prostration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r16.anchor: وذهب الشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق إلى أنه يكبر ويرفع اليدين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r17.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r17.claim: Mālik says to say the takbīr when descending; raising the hands is done in prayer, while reports differ about doing so outside prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r17.anchor: وقال مالك يكبر لها في الخفض، والرفع في الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r18.claim: The majority say to end with salām; a group of early authorities and Isḥāq say there is no salām.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r18.anchor: ويسلم عند الجمهور، وقال جماعة من السلف وإسحاق: لا يسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r19.speaker: الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r19.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and a group permit recitation prostration at any time because it is a prayer with a specific cause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r19.anchor: ووقتها سائر الأوقات مطلقا لأنها صلاة بسبب وهو قول الشافعي وجماعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r20.claim: Other views forbid it after sunrise until the sun is high, after dawn and afternoon prayers, or only after dawn; these three positions occur in Mālik's school.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p264/r20.anchor: وقيل: ما لم يسفر ولم تصفر الشمس، وقيل: لا يسجد بعد الصبح ولا بعد العصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p265/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p265/r1.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p265/r1.claim: The well-known Mālikī position is that one does not perform recitation prostration during an obligatory prayer, whether recited silently or aloud.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p265/r1.anchor: ومشهور مذهب مالك أنه لا يسجد في الفريضة سرا كانت أو جهرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p265/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p265/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p265/r2.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa requires prostration from a listener who initially intended to listen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p265/r2.anchor: ومذهب أبي حنيفة أنه واجب على السامع قصد الاستماع أولا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r1.claim: Those “near your Lord” are the angels of the highest assembly; nearness means rank and divine favor, not place, since God is transcendent.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r1.anchor: وهم ملائكة الملأ الأعلى فالمراد من العندية القرب من الله تعالى بالزلفى والرضا لا المكانية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes “near your Lord” to mean near the Lord’s Throne.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : المراد عند عرش ربك لايستكبرون

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r3.claim: The angels perform worship as they have been commanded.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r3.anchor: لايستكبرون عن عبادته ( بل يؤدونها حسبما أمروا به

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r4.claim: Their glorification declares God utterly free of whatever does not befit His majestic presence.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r4.anchor: ينزهونه عما لا يليق بحضرة كبريائه على أبلغ وجه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r5.claim: They devote ultimate servitude and humility to God alone and associate no one with Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r5.anchor: ويخصونه بغاية العبودية والتذلل لا يشركون به غيره جل شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r6.claim: The fronted “to Him” indirectly reproaches other morally responsible beings who fail to worship as the angels do.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r7.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r7.claim: Al-Ṭībī reads the whole statement as a rationale: worship sincerely as commanded, since God has honored servants and needs neither people nor their worship; fronting also serves the verse ending.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r7.anchor: كما آثره العلامة الطيبي لأنه تعليل للسابق على معنى ائتوا بالعبادة على وجه الإخلاص

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r8.claim: The prostration at this verse may follow a commanded prostration, oppose unbelievers’ refusal, or imitate prophets’ prostration; this instance fits the latter two explanations through allusion or explicit mention.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r8.anchor: وقد جاء الأمر بالسجدة لآية أمر فيها بالسجود امتثالا للأمر أو حكى فيها إستنكاف الكفرة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports a Prophetic supplication in prostration asking God for beneficial knowledge and deeds that raise one’s rank.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r9.anchor: عن ابن عمر اللهم لك سجد سوادي وبك آمن فؤادي اللهم ارزقني علما ينفعني

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r10.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r10.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet repeatedly said during night recitation prostrations, “My face prostrates to its Creator”; the Tirmidhī report is graded authentic by al-Tirmidhī.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r10.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وأبو داود والترمذي وصححه عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r11.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r11.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that each Muslim prostration raises a degree, removes a sin, or grants both.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r11.anchor: وجاء عنها أيضا ما من مسلم سجد لله تعالى سجدة إلا رفعه الله تعالى بها درجة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r12.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Satan weeps when Adam’s child prostrates and gains Paradise, while Satan refused and faces the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r12.anchor: وأخرج مسلم وابن ماجة والبيهقي عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r13.claim: Al-Ālūsī infers that quiet remembrance is preferable and supports this with Aḥmad’s report, “The best remembrance is silent.”
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r13.anchor: استدل بالآية على أن إخفاء الذكر أفضل

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r14.claim: He condemns the religiously, rationally, and conventionally objectionable practices of ignorant Sufis of his time.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r14.anchor: وهي ناعية على جهلة زماننا من المتصوفة ما يفعلونه مما يستقبح شرعا وعقلا وعرفا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r17.claim: In the inward reading, those near God are annihilated and abiding through Him, established in spiritual uprightness; they have no ego-claim, glorify by negating it, and prostrate through complete self-effacement, for God alone remains.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p156#2/r17.anchor: وهم الفانون الباقون به سبحانه وتعالى أرباب الإستقامة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r1.speaker: جماعة من السلف
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r1.claim: A group of early authorities treated al-Anfal and Bara'a as one surah, which they saw as explaining their arrangement.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r1.anchor: قال جماعة من السلف : أنهما سورة واحدة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r2.claim: One rationale for placing Bara'a here is its length: among the six preceding surahs, none is longer, which is enough to establish affinity.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r2.anchor: وضع براءة هنا لمناسبة الطول فإنه ليس بعد الست السابقة سورة أطول منها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r3.claim: A third rationale says placing the pair amid the seven long surahs, whose order was known early, signals that their placement was not fixed by revelation and that the Prophet died before explaining them.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r3.anchor: خلل بالسورتين أثناء السبع الطول المعلوم ترتيبها في العصر الأول للإشارة إلى أن ذلك أمر صادر لا عن توقيف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r4.claim: Al-Alusi calls the non-tawqifi explanation very far-fetched, citing his earlier discussion; the question to the Jewish scholar and Uthman's answer do not explicitly establish it.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r4.anchor: ما ذكره من عدم التوقيف في هذا الوضع في غاية البعد كما يفهم مما قدمناه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r5.claim: A fourth arrangement proposal would move Yunus ahead and place Hud after Bara'a, as in Ubayy's codex, to preserve the seven-long sequence.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r5.anchor: لو أخرهما وقدم يونس وأتى بعد براءة بهود كما في مصحف أبي لمراعاة مناسبة السبع

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r6.claim: Yunus has a stronger connection with the next five surahs through shared stories, alif-lam-ra openings, mention of the Book, Meccan origin, comparable length apart from al-Hijr, and names of prophets; al-Ra'd is a fitting angelic name alongside them.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r6.anchor: الأولى بسورة يونس أن يؤتى بالسور الخمس التي بعدها لما اشتركت فيه من المناسبات من القصص والإفتتاح

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r7.claim: These multiple links between Yunus and the following surahs outweigh the single consideration for placing Yunus immediately after al-A'raf.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r7.anchor: وهي آكد من هذا الوجه الواحد في تقديم يونس بعد الأعراف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r8.claim: The same links partly explain placing al-Hijr before al-Nahl despite its shorter length; moving Bara'a after six shorter surahs would make the connection much weaker because Bara'a is exceptionally long.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r8.anchor: ولو أخرت براءة عن هذه السور الست لبعدت المناسبة جدا لطولها بعد عدة سور أقصر منها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r9.claim: Surah openings help explain placing al-Hijr before al-Nahl and Aal Imran before al-Nisa, but this opening-based rationale is not consistent throughout the Quran's arrangement.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r9.anchor: يشهد لمراعاة الفواتح في مناسبة الوضع ما ذكرناه من تقديم الحجر على النحل

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r10.claim: Ibn Mas'ud's codex placed the seven long surahs in descending length, then the hundred-verse surahs similarly, with Anfal after al-Nur.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r10.anchor: أن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه قدم في مصحفه البقرة والنساء وآل عمران والأعراف والأنعام والمائدة ويونس راعى السبع الطول

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r11.claim: The placement of Anfal after al-Nur links al-Nur's promise that believers will inherit the land with Anfal's reminder of their earlier weakness, presenting the promised outcome as fulfilled.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r11.anchor: فإن الأولى مشتملة على الوعد بما حصل وذكر به في الثانية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r12.speaker: عثمان
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r12.claim: Al-Nahhas reports from Uthman that Anfal and Bara'a were called the twin surahs in the Prophet's time, so he placed them among the seven long surahs.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r12.anchor: أخرج النحاس في ناسخه عنه أنه قال : كانت الأنفال وبراءة يدعيان في زمن رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r13.claim: The identity of the seventh long surah is disputed: Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr, and one Ibn Abbas report say Yunus; another report from Ibn Abbas in al-Hakim says al-Kahf; other scholars end the set with Bara'a, while another view counts Anfal and Bara'a together.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r13.anchor: ليس أمرا مجمعا عليه بل هو قول مجاهد وابن جبير ورواية عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r14.claim: Al-Alusi says the question to the Jewish scholar and Uthman's reply are not explicit evidence that the surah placement was not divinely fixed.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r14.anchor: وسؤال الحبر وجواب عثمان رضي الله تعالى عنهما ليسا نصا في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r15.claim: Al-Alusi says the earlier scholar's first proposed rationale conflicts with the apparent question, which suggests omission of the basmala from Bara'a was itself a matter of judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r15.anchor: في أول الأمور التي فتح الله تعالى بها عليه غير ملائم بظاهره ظاهر سؤال الحبر رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r16.claim: Al-Alusi says God granted him an explanation of this surah's connection to the preceding one that the earlier eminent scholar had not supplied.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p158/r16.anchor: قد من الله تعالى على هذا العبد الحقير بما لم يمن به على هذا الجليل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r1.claim: Those near their Lord are the angels, distinguished by merit and honor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r1.anchor: {إن الذين عند ربك} يعني: الملائكة المقربين بالفضل والكرامة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r2.claim: لا يستكبرون means they do not act proudly.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r3.claim: They declare God transcendent and remember Him, saying “Glory be to God.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r3.anchor: {عن عبادته ويسبحونه} وينزهونه ويذكرونه، فيقولون: سبحان الله.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says that when a person recites a prostration verse and prostrates, Satan withdraws weeping, saying the human obeyed and gains Paradise while he disobeyed and faces the Fire.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا قرأ ابن آدم السجدة فسجد اعتزل الشيطان يبكي، فيقول: يا ويله أمر هذا بالسجود فسجد فله الجنة وأمرت بالسجود فعصيت فلي النار"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r5.speaker: ثوبان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r5.claim: Thawban reports the Prophet saying each prostration to God raises a servant one degree and removes one sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p321#2/r5.anchor: عن معدان قال: سألت ثوبان مولى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قلت: حدثني حديثا ينفعني الله به، قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "ما من عبد يسجد لله سجدة إلا رفعه الله بها درجة وحط عنه بها سيئة"

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r7.claim: Those near their Lord are the angels of the highest assembly.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r7.anchor: إن الذين عند ربك } يعني ملائكة الملأ الأعلى

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r8.claim: They do not disdain worship and declare God’s transcendence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r8.anchor: لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ويسبحونه } وينزهونه

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r9.claim: Their prostration is exclusive worship and submission to God, without associating anything with Him.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r10.claim: The angels’ conduct reproaches other accountable beings, and prostration is prescribed when this verse is recited.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r10.anchor: وهو تعريض بمن عداهم من المكلفين ولذلك شرع السجود

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r11.claim: A prophetic report says Satan withdraws weeping when a human recites a prostration verse and prostrates, since the human obeyed and earns Paradise while Satan disobeyed and earns Fire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r11.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:205-206/r12.claim: A prophetic report says reciting Sūrat al-Aʿrāf earns a screen between the reciter and Iblis on Judgment Day, with Adam interceding for the reciter.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r11.claim: Those near their Lord are the pure, protected angels; their nearness is rank and station, not physical location.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r11.anchor: وهم الملائكة الكرام أولو العصمة , والقرب دنو مكانة لا مكان

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r12.claim: They neither display nor seek pride in worship, despite their closeness, purity, and love.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r12.anchor: أي لا يوجدون ولا يطلبون الكبر

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r13.claim: Their tasbīḥ declares God free of everything unfitting, and their purity removes the pull of desire and self-interest.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r13.anchor: أي ينزهونه عن كل مالا يليق

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r14.claim: The angels reserve prostration for God, combining affirmation of His perfection with direct bodily worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r14.anchor: أي يخضعون بإثباتهم له كل كمال

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r15.claim: The verse gives three angelic traits: freedom from pride, glorification, and exclusive prostration; inward glorification and bodily prostration represent heart and physical worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r15.anchor: وقد تضمنت الآية الإخبار عن الملائكة الأبرار بثلاثة أخبار : عدم الاستكبار الذي هو أجل أنواع العبادة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r16.claim: He invokes the saying that a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating; Abū Ḥayyān notes that both forms of worship ultimately return to the heart, one signaled by speech and the other by action.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r16.anchor: ( أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد ) نبه عليه أبو حيان على أن العبادتين مرجعهما القلب

BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r17.claim: The angels’ humility and regular submission contrast with Iblīs’s arrogant refusal to prostrate to Adam; the surah’s conclusion also returns to its opening command to follow the Qur’an.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p178/r17.anchor: إلى وصف إبليس بعصيان أمر الله في السجود لآدم عليه السلام

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1648#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1648#2/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1648#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi glosses their glorification as prayer.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r1.claim: This sentence gives the reason for the command to remember God: believers should emulate the perfect beings of the heavenly assembly, while the contrast reproaches polytheists who disdain worship.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r2.claim: Those ‘near your Lord’ are angels; their worship is a model because the human Messenger’s rank approaches theirs through his mission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r2.anchor: والمراد ب { الذين عند ربك } الملائكة ، ووجه جعل حال الملائكة علة لأمر النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r3.claim: The comparison does not imply that angels outrank prophets, as the Muʿtazilites assume: humans’ acquired imitation of angelic traits is more remarkable and more deserving of merit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r3.anchor: فليس في هذا التعليل ما يقتضي أن يكون الملائكة أفضل من الرسل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r4.claim: The clause’s emphatic in functions like a consequence marker and supplies a reason for repeated remembrance in different circumstances, not a response to doubt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r4.anchor: ويفيد التعليل كما تقدم غير مرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r5.claim: Ibn Dāra’s couplet illustrates the exhortation to emulate a model: when a group does good, its like has already done good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r5.anchor: كقول ابن دارة سالم بن مسافع : فإن تتقوا شرا فمثلكم اتقى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r6.claim: Replacing the word ‘angels’ with a relative clause signals their elevated station and encourages competition in adopting their conduct.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r6.anchor: ووجه العدول عن لفظ الملائكة إلى الموصولية : ما تؤذن به الصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r7.claim: ‘Near’ is figurative for high rank and divine favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243/r7.anchor: و { عند } مستعمل مجازا في رفعة المقدار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r1.claim: Mentioning that angels do not disdain worship primarily hints at the polytheists’ opposite conduct, rather than serving as the strongest praise of angels.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r1.anchor: ليس المقصود به التنويه بشأن الملائكة لأن التنويه بهم يكون بأفضل من ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r2.claim: The intended rationale is their glorification: they declare God free of deficient attributes in speech and belief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r2.anchor: أي ينزهونه بالقول والاعتقاد عن صفات النقص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r3.claim: The imperfect form conveys renewed and continuing glorification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r3.anchor: واختيار صيغة المضارع لدلالتها على التجديد والاستمرار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r4.claim: Fronting ‘to Him’ makes the prostration exclusive to God, indirectly censuring polytheists who prostrate to others; the imperfect also signals continuity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r4.anchor: للدلالة على الاختصاص أي ولا يسجدون لغيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r5.claim: This is a Qurʾanic prostration site, the first in mushaf order, and scholars of the community agree that prostration is prescribed here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r5.anchor: من المتفق على السجود فيه بين علماء الأمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r6.claim: The prostration urges imitation of the angels; once their worship is described, the Prophet hastens to prostrate in order to realize the passage’s aim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r6.anchor: أن الآية جاءت للحض على التخلق بأخلاق الملائكة في الذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r7.claim: After the polytheists asked for a sign and were told to follow revelation and listen to the Qurʾan, this prostration distinguishes believers who prostrate from attending polytheists who refuse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r7.anchor: وبأن يأمرهم بالاستماع للقرآن وذكر أن الملائكة يسجدون لله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Qurʾanic prostration sites serve to frustrate polytheists or to imitate prophets; he links David’s prostration to the command that Muhammad follow prophetic guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p243#2/r8.anchor: كما قال ابن عباس في سجدة ، { فاستغفر ربه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r4.claim: “Those who are with your Lord” refers to the angels.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r5.claim: Their being “with” God means rank, honor, and nearness in status, not physical location.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r5.anchor: وقوله عند إنما يريد في المنزلة والتشريف والقرب في المكانة لا في المكان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r6.claim: The angels are humble and persist in worship, glorification, and prostration.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r6.anchor: ثم وصف تعالى حالهم من تواضعهم وإدمانهم للعبادة والتسبيح والسجود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r7.claim: A Prophetic report says the sky groans, rightly, because no space the size of a handspan is without a standing, bowing, or prostrating angel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث: أطت السماء وحق لها أن تئط ما فيها موضع شبر إلا وفيه ملك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r8.speaker: النخعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r8.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī, in the book of al-Naqqāsh, says one may either bow or prostrate at this verse’s prostration marker.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p495/r8.anchor: قال النخعي في كتاب النقاش: إن شئت ركعت وإن شئت سجدت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r1.claim: Those who are near their Lord are the angels.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r1.anchor: يعني الملائكة ﴿ لا يستكبرون ﴾ أي لا يتكبرون ويتعظمون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r2.claim: They do not act arrogantly or exalt themselves.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r2.anchor: أي لا يتكبرون ويتعظمون ﴿ عن عبادته ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r3.claim: One explanation of their worship is obedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r3.anchor: وفي هذه العبادة قولان أحدهما الطاعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r4.claim: Another explanation of their worship is prayer and humility within it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r5.claim: One explanation of their glorification is that they declare God free of evil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r5.anchor: قولان أحدهما ينزهونه عن السوء والثاني يقولون سبحان الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r6.claim: Another explanation is that they say Subhan Allah.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r7.claim: Their prostration means that they pray.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r7.anchor: ﴿ وله يسجدون ﴾ أي يصلون وقيل سبب نزول هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r8.claim: The verse was revealed after Meccan unbelievers asked whether they should prostrate as commanded; it points out that higher-ranking angels do not disdain God's worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r8.anchor: وقيل سبب نزول هذه الآية أن كفار مكة قالوا أنسجد لما تأمرنا فنزلت هذه الآية تخبر أن الملائكة وهم أكبر شأنا منكم لا يتكبرون عن عبادة الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r9.speaker: النبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when a person recites a prostration verse and prostrates, Satan withdraws weeping: the person obeyed and earns Paradise, while Satan disobeyed and faces Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p314#2/r9.anchor: وقد روى أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إذا قرأ ابن آدم السجدة فسجد اعتزل الشيطان يبكي ويقول يا ويله أمر هذا بالسجود فسجد فله الجنة وأمرت بالسجود فعصيت فلي النار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r10.claim: The angels near their Lord do not disdain worship; they glorify Him continually and prostrate, and their mention invites believers to emulate their abundant devotion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r10.anchor: وإنما ذكرهم بهذا ليتشبه بهم في كثرة طاعتهم وعبادتهم؛ ولهذا شرع لنا السجود هاهنا لما ذكر سجودهم لله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r11.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a hadith urging Muslims to line up as angels do, complete the first rows, and stand close together.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p538/r11.anchor: "ألا تصفون كما تصف الملائكة عند ربها، يتمون الصفوف الأول، ويتراصون في الصف"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p539/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p539/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p539/r1.claim: This is the first prostration of recitation in the Qur'an; reciters and listeners are unanimously to prostrate at it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p539/r1.anchor: وهذه أول سجدة في القرآن، مما يشرع لتاليها ومستمعها السجود بالإجماع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p539/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p539/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p539/r2.claim: A report from Abu al-Darda says the Prophet counted this verse among the Qur'an's prostrations.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p539/r2.anchor: وقد ورد في حديث رواه ابن ماجه، عن أبي الدرداء، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه عدها في سجدات القرآن

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r8.claim: Istikbār is seeking great rank by refusing the truth; the form istifʿāl originally conveys seeking.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r8.anchor: والاستكبار: طلب كبر القدر بالامتناع من الحق، وهو استفعال من الكبر،

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r9.claim: Tasbīḥ is declaring God transcendent above attributes that cannot properly be ascribed to Him.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r9.anchor: والتسبيح لله: هو التنزيه له عما لا يجوز عليه.

JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r11.claim: After the preceding command to recite and listen to the Quran, these verses explain the manner of remembrance and supplication.
JISHUMI:v4p2834#2/r11.anchor: لما تقدم الأمر بقراءة القرآن والاستماع، بين كيفية القراءة وكيفية الدعاء، فقال سبحانه: واذكر ربك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r1.claim: Those near their Lord are the angels; ‘near’ means nearness in rank and closeness to God’s mercy and favor through their obedience and pursuit of His pleasure.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r2.claim: They reserve worship exclusively for God and associate no one with Him, implicitly rebuking other morally responsible beings.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r2.anchor: ويختصونه بالعبادة لا يشركون به غيره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet promises that reciting Sūrat al-Aʿrāf will place a screen between the reciter and Iblīs on Judgment Day, with Adam interceding for the reciter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p182/r3.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r12.claim: This is the first prostration of recitation in the Qur’an.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r12.anchor: وهذا أول سجدات التلاوة في القرآن

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r13.speaker: كفار مكة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r13.claim: Meccan disbelievers objected, “What is the Merciful? Shall we prostrate to what you command?”; God then revealed this verse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r13.anchor: وسبب نزولها ما قاله كفار مكة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r14.claim: If even the angels brought near submit with humility and longing, people are still more entitled to do so.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p290#2/r14.anchor: إذا كانوا على هذه الحال في الخضوع والرغبة فأنتم بذلك أولى

MUQATIL:7:205-206/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:205-206/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:205-206/r3.claim: The angels are mentioned in response to Meccan unbelievers asking what the Merciful is and whether they should prostrate to what the Prophet commands, as in 25:60.
MUQATIL:7:205-206/r3.anchor: وذلك حين قال كفار مكة: وما الرحمن أنسجد لما تأمرنا

MUQATIL:7:205-206/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:205-206/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:205-206/r4.claim: Unlike the Meccan unbelievers, the angels are not arrogant about worshipping God; they glorify Him by remembering Him and prostrate by praying.
MUQATIL:7:205-206/r4.anchor: { لا يستكبرون } ، يعنى لا يتكبرون { عن عبادته } كفعل كفار مكة، وأخبر عن الملائكة، فقال: { ويسبحونه }

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r1.claim: Those «with your Lord» are the angels, with Him in rank and station, not physical location.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r1.anchor: مكانة ومنزلة لا مكانا ونزلا يعنى الملائكة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r2.claim: The angels do not deem themselves too exalted for worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r2.anchor: لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ﴾ الأعراف 195 تعظمون عنها

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r3.claim: They glorify God by declaring Him free of what is unbefitting.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r4.claim: They reserve prostration and worship for God and associate no one with Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p53#5/r4.anchor: ويختصونه بالعبادة لا يشركون به غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r1.claim: The angels are unanimously identified as those near their Lord.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains nearness to God as nearness to His mercy; anyone near His mercy is described as with Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r2.anchor: كل قريب من رحمة الله عز وجل فهو عنده عن الزجاج

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r3.speaker: غيره
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r3.claim: Another explanation says the angels are with God because they are in a place reached only by His decree.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r3.anchor: وقال غيره: لأنهم في موضع لا ينفذ فيه إلا حكم الله

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r4.claim: Another explanation describes the angels as God’s messengers, like saying a king has many troops at his court.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r4.anchor: وقيل: لأنهم رسل الله كما يقال: عند الخليفة جيش كثير

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r5.claim: Another view makes this nearness honorific: it denotes rank, not physical distance.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r5.anchor: وقيل: هذا على جهة التشريف لهم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r6.claim: The angels glorify God by exalting Him and declaring Him free of every evil.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r7.claim: One interpretation takes their prostration to mean that they pray.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r8.claim: Another interprets prostration as humble submission, unlike the behavior of sinners.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r9.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r9.claim: The majority hold that this verse is a place where a Qurʾān reciter performs the prostration of recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r9.anchor: والجمهور من العلماء في أن هذا موضع سجود للقارىء

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r10.speaker: ابن حبيب وابن وهب وإسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r10.claim: One count gives fifteen prostrations, from the end of al-Aʿrāf through the end of al-ʿAlaq; this is Ibn Ḥabīb, one report from Ibn Wahb, and Isḥāq’s view.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r10.anchor: وهو قول ابن حبيب وابن وهب في رواية وإسحاق

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r11.speaker: بعض العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r11.claim: Some add the prostration at 15:98, making sixteen.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r11.anchor: ومن العلماء من زاد سجدة الحجر قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r12.speaker: ابن وهب
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r12.claim: Another report from Ibn Wahb counts fourteen, omitting the second al-Ḥajj prostration; this is the Ḥanafī position.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r12.anchor: وقيل: أربع عشرة قاله ابن وهب في الرواية الأخرى عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r13.claim: Al-Qurṭubī considers omitting the second al-Ḥajj prostration correct because the report establishing it is not sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r13.anchor: والصحيح سقوطها لأن الحديث لم يصح بثبوتها

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r14.speaker: عبد الله بن منين
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r14.claim: A report to ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ says the Prophet taught fifteen prostrations, including three in al-Mufaṣṣal and two in al-Ḥajj; ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq says Ibn Munayn is not a reliable proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r14.anchor: ورواه ابن ماجه وأبو داود في سننهما عن عبد الله بن منين من بني عبد كلال

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r15.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r15.claim: Abū Dāwūd reports ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir asking whether al-Ḥajj has two prostrations; the Prophet says yes, but Ibn Lahīʿah in its chain is very weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r15.anchor: عقبة بن عامر قال قلت: يا رسول الله، أفي سورة الحج سجدتان

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r16.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r16.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī counts both al-Ḥajj prostrations and omits the prostration in Ṣād.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r17.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r17.claim: The famous Mālikī count is eleven, omitting the last al-Ḥajj prostration and three in al-Mufaṣṣal; it is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r17.anchor: وهو مشهور مذهب مالك. وروي عن ابن عباس وابن عمر وغيرهما

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r18.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r18.claim: Ibn Mājah reports Abū al-Dardāʾ saying he prostrated with the Prophet eleven times, listing al-Aʿrāf, al-Raʿd, al-Naḥl, Banī Isrāʾīl, Maryam, one in al-Ḥajj, al-Furqān, al-Naml, al-Sajdah, Ṣād, and one of the Ḥawāmīm.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r18.anchor: وفي سنن ابن ماجه عن أبي الدرداء قال: سجدت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إحدى عشرة سجدة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r19.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r19.claim: Another count attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās is ten, omitting the last al-Ḥajj prostration, Ṣād, and the three in al-Mufaṣṣal.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r19.anchor: وقيل: عشر، وأسقط آخرة الحج وص وثلاث المفصل ذكر عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r20.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r20.claim: A further count is four: al-Sajdah, Ḥā Mīm al-Sajdah, al-Najm, and al-ʿAlaq.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r20.anchor: وقيل: إنها أربع، سجدة آلم تنزيل وحم تنزيل والنجم والعلق

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r21.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r21.claim: Counts differ because reports and practice vary, and scholars disagree whether Qurʾānic commands to prostrate mean recitation prostration or required prayer prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r21.anchor: وسبب الخلاف اختلاف النقل في الأحاديث والعمل

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r22.speaker: مالك والشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206/r22.claim: Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī hold that prostration of recitation is not obligatory.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r1.claim: Abū Ḥanīfah holds recitation prostration obligatory, citing the unqualified command, reports about Satan weeping when Adam’s child prostrates and about Paradise and Hell, and the Prophet’s practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r1.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: هو واجب. وتعلق بأن مطلق الأمر بالسجود على الوجوب

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r2.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r2.claim: Al-Qurṭubī relies on the sound report that ʿUmar prostrated after reciting a sajdah, then later said God had not made it obligatory unless people chose.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r2.anchor: حديث عمر الثابت خرجه البخاري أنه قرأ آية سجدة على المنبر

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r3.claim: ʿUmar’s statement before the Companions, without objection, establishes consensus that recitation prostration is not obligatory.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r3.anchor: فلم ينكر عليه أحد فثبت الإجماع به في ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r4.claim: The report that Adam’s child was commanded to prostrate refers to an obligatory prostration; the Prophet’s regular practice indicates recommendation.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r4.anchor: فإخبار عن السجود الواجب. ومواظبة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تدل على الاستحباب

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r5.claim: Recitation prostration requires prayer’s conditions: purity, intention, qibla, and a permissible time; Ibn ʿUmar and al-Shaʿbī are reported to allow it without purity.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r5.anchor: ولا خلاف في أن سجود القرآن يحتاج إلى ما تحتاج إليه الصلاة من طهارة حدث ونجس

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r6.claim: Al-Bukhārī reports Ibn ʿUmar prostrating without purity; Ibn al-Mundhir reports the same of al-Shaʿbī.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r6.anchor: ذكر البخاري عن ابن عمر أنه كان يسجد على غير طهارة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r7.speaker: الشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r7.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and Isḥāq require takbīr and raising the hands for prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r7.anchor: فذهب الشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق إلى أنه يكبر ويرفع للتكبير لها

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r8.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUmar says the Prophet said takbīr when prostrating and rising.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا سجد كبر

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r9.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r9.claim: Mālik’s well-known position is takbīr on lowering and rising inside prayer; views differ on takbīr outside prayer, though most jurists require it.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r9.anchor: مشهور مذهب مالك أنه يكبر لها في الخفض والرفع في الصلاة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r10.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r10.claim: The majority do not require salām after recitation prostration, while a group of early authorities and Isḥāq require it.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#2/r10.anchor: ولا سلام لها عند الجمهور. وذهب جماعة من السلف وإسحاق إلى أنه يسلم منها

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r1.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī prefers requiring salām: an act with takbīr should have an exit like prayer; this is even more fitting than for funeral prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r1.anchor: وهذه عبادة لها تكبير، فكان لها تحليل كصلاة الجنازة بل أولى، لأنها فعل وصلاة الجنازة قول. وهذا اختيار ابن العربي

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r2.speaker: الشافعي وجماعة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r2.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī and a group allow prostration at any time because it is prayer for a specific cause.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r2.anchor: يسجد في سائر الأوقات مطلقا لأنها صلاة لسبب. وهو قول الشافعي وجماعة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r3.claim: One view permits prostration until dawn brightens or until the sun yellows after ʿAṣr.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r3.anchor: ما لم يسفر الصبح، أو ما لم تصفر الشمس بعد العصر

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r4.claim: Another view forbids prostration after both dawn and ʿAṣr.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r4.anchor: لا يسجد بعد الصبح ولا بعد العصر

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r5.claim: A further view allows it after dawn but not after ʿAṣr; these positions occur in the Mālikī school.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r5.anchor: يسجد بعد الصبح ولا يسجد بعد العصر. وهذه الثلاثة الأقوال في مذهبنا

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r6.claim: Timing opinions balance recitation prostration against the general ban on prayer after ʿAṣr and dawn, and differ on that ban’s rationale.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r6.anchor: سبب الخلاف معارضة ما يقتضيه سبب قراءة السجدة من السجود المرتب عليها

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās transmits from the Prophet a supplication asking God to remove a burden, record reward, and store it as a treasure.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r7.anchor: رواه ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكره ابن ماجه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r8.claim: In voluntary prayer, prostrate alone or in a congregation when disruption is not feared; the stated ruling permits prostration even if feared, though another view forbids that.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r8.anchor: فإن كان في نافلة سجد إن كان منفردا أو في جماعة وأمن التخليط فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r9.claim: A view says not to prostrate in voluntary congregational prayer when it may confuse the congregation.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r10.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r10.claim: Mālik’s well-known position forbids recitation prostration in obligatory prayer, whether quiet or aloud and alone or in a congregation, as an extra prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r10.anchor: المشهور عن مالك النهي عنه فيها، سواء كانت صلاة سر أو جهر

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r11.speaker: قيل
