QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r11.claim: Another explanation is fear of confusing the congregation; on this rationale it is allowed alone or where confusion is unlikely.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r11.anchor: وقيل: معلل بخوف التخليط على الجماعة وهذا أشبه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r12.speaker: أبو رافع
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r12.claim: Al-Bukhārī alone reports Abū Rāfiʿ praying ʿIshāʾ with Abū Hurayrah, who prostrated at al-Inshiqāq and said he had done so behind the Prophet and would continue until meeting him.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r12.anchor: روى البخاري عن أبي رافع قال: صليت مع أبي هريرة العتمة، فقرأ

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r13.speaker: عمران بن حصين
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r13.claim: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn’s answer about a person who hears a prostration but was not seated for it implies the listener is not obliged to prostrate.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r13.anchor: وقيل لعمران بن حصين: الرجل يسمع السجدة ولم يجلس لها

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r14.speaker: سلمان
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r14.claim: Salmān said, “We did not come for this,” regarding recitation prostration.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r15.speaker: عثمان
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r15.claim: ʿUthmān held that prostration is due only from someone who listens attentively.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r15.anchor: وقال عثمان: إنما السجدة على من استمعها

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r16.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r16.claim: Al-Zuhrī requires purity; at home face the qibla, while a mounted traveler may face any direction.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r16.anchor: وقال الزهري: لا يسجد إلا أن يكون طاهرا

QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r17.speaker: السائب
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r17.claim: Al-Sāʾib did not prostrate when a preacher prostrated.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:206#3/r17.anchor: وكان السائب لا يسجد لسجود القاص

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r1.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r1.claim: Al-Kashifi reports that Meccan unbelievers disliked prostration and asked whether they should prostrate to what Muhammad commanded, increasing in aversion.
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r1.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (آورده اندكه كفار مكة تعظم ميكردند

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r2.claim: Those near their Lord are the angels, near by honor and rank rather than by distance or place.
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r2.anchor: الملائكة المقربين لديه قرب الشرف والمكانة لاقرب المسافة والمكان

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r3.claim: The angels do not disdain worship but carry it out as commanded; their glorification declares God free of anything unworthy of His majesty.

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r4.claim: Placing lahu before the verb conveys exclusivity: they direct the utmost servitude and humility to God alone, without associating anything with Him.

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r5.claim: The angels’ exclusive prostration indirectly reproaches other accountable beings; this is why prostration of recitation is prescribed at this verse.

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r6.claim: Prostration is the ultimate humility; it is prescribed in some places to remedy deficiency, as in forgetfulness prostration, and in others to oppose unbelievers and follow Muslims.
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r6.anchor: السجدة نهاية الخضوع وإنما شرعت في موضع جبرا للنقصان كسجود السهو

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r7.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r7.claim: Al-Kashifi counts twelve prostrations of recitation; Shafi‘i and Ahmad recognize one at the end of al-Hajj, while Imam Abu Hanifa does not.
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r7.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (سجده تلاوت هارده موضع است در قرآن

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r8.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r8.claim: For surah Sad, Abu Hanifa counts a recitation prostration because the Prophet prostrated there; the other imams do not, since the passage mentions bowing, not prostration.
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r8.anchor: بمذهب امام أعظم هست لأن النبي عليه السلام قرأ سورة ص وسجد وبمذهب باقي ائمه نه

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r9.speaker: علي
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r9.claim: Ali places the Fussilat prostration at the words إن كنتم إياه تعبدون; al-Shafi‘i follows this position.
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r9.anchor: فعند علي رضي الله عنه هو قوله : {إن كنتم

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r10.speaker: عمر وابن مسعود
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r10.claim: Umar and Ibn Masud place the Fussilat prostration at لا يسأمون; Bursevi follows them as a precaution because delaying is permissible but doing it early is not.
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r10.anchor: وعند عمر وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما هو قوله : {لا يسامون}

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r11.claim: For Abu Hanifa, prostration of recitation is immediately obligatory on reciter and listener, inside or outside prayer, and must be made up if missed; the other imams call it sunnah without make-up.
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r11.anchor: ونزد امام أعظم سجده تلاوت برخواننده وشنونده درنماز وغير نماز واجبست

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r12.claim: Unnecessary delay is disliked; the seated worshipper should rise with takbir, recite the prayer’s glorification, prostrate with takbir, then sit, since this makes the prostration fuller.
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r12.anchor: ويكره تأخير السجدة من غير ضرورة ويستحب أن يقوم القاعد فيكبر ويسبح تسبيح الصلاة

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r13.claim: The preferred glorification is سبحان ربي الأعلى three times; alternatives are خضعت للرحمن فاغفر لي يا رحمن and يا مقلب القلوب ثبت قلبي على دينك, favored by the author of al-Asrar al-Muhammadiyya.
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r13.anchor: وهو الأصح وقيل يقول : "خضعت للرحمن فاغفر لي يا رحمن"

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r14.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r14.claim: The Prophet said in recitation prostration that his face prostrated to its Creator, who formed it and gave it hearing and sight by His power, then prayed for reward, pardon, provision, and acceptance.
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r14.anchor: وكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول في سجود التلاوة "سجد وجهي للذي خلقه

BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r15.speaker: ابن فخر الدين الرومي
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r15.claim: Ibn Fakhr al-Din al-Rumi recommends distinct supplications for the prostrations in al-Isra, al-Araf or al-Sajda, and al-Najm, asking for praise, humility, and protection from pride.
BURSEVI:v3p235#2/r15.anchor: قال ابن فخر الدين الرومي إن قرأ سجدة سبحان ضم إليها ما ذكره سبحانه

BURSEVI:v3p237/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p237/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p237/r1.claim: Persian verses shame the person who turns away from prostration and present obedience through prostration as the fitting path.
BURSEVI:v3p237/r1.anchor: توكنى از سجده او سر كشى به كه ازين شيوه قدم در كشى

BURSEVI:v3p237/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p237/r2.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
BURSEVI:v3p237/r2.claim: The Shaykh al-Islam’s Persian maxim praises prostration and censures a head that is absent from it.
BURSEVI:v3p237/r2.anchor: وحشرت شيخ الإسلام قدس سره فرموده سرى كه دروسجودي نيست

BURSEVI:v3p237/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p237/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p237/r3.claim: A Persian couplet says the soul’s nobility comes through generosity and honor through prostration; lacking both makes one’s existence worse than nonexistence.

BURSEVI:v3p237/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p237/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمة
BURSEVI:v3p237/r4.claim: The people near God have effaced their actions, traits, and selves in God’s commands, qualities, and essence; they no longer remain in themselves but through God.
BURSEVI:v3p237/r4.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمة" : {إن الذين عند ربك} يعني

BURSEVI:v3p237/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p237/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p237/r5.claim: Bursevi continues Najmiyya’s account: because the saints effaced pride and their own actions, they do not disdain worship; in self-annihilation and abiding in God, their acts are worship rather than independent action.
BURSEVI:v3p237/r5.anchor: لأن الاستكبار من أخلاقهم وقد أفنوها في أخلاقه

BURSEVI:v3p237#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p237#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p237#2/r1.claim: God is transcendent beyond indwelling, union, or fusion, and beyond claims that God is the servant or the servant God; He remains as He was in eternity.
BURSEVI:v3p237#2/r1.anchor: ينزهونه عن الحلول والاتصال والاتحاد وعن أن يكون هو العبد والعبد إياه

BURSEVI:v3p237#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p237#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p237#2/r2.claim: All beings bowed before God in pre-eternal nonexistence, submitting to His power to bring them into existence; in existence they surrender what they have to His decrees of annihilation, creation, and preservation.
BURSEVI:v3p237#2/r2.anchor: في الوجود والعدم من الأزل والأبد سجدوا له من الأزل في العدم منقادين مسخرين

BURSEVI:v3p237#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p237#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p237#2/r3.claim: Bursevi records the completion of al-Araf’s commentary in the first ten days of Safar 1101 AH and says al-Anfal follows.
BURSEVI:v3p237#2/r3.anchor: تمت سورة الأعراف بالرحم والراف مع ما يتعلق بها من التفسير والتأويل

RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r1.claim: After urging the Messenger to remember God, the verse points to the angels’ constant worship: despite their honor, purity, and freedom from passions, they persist in obedience, so embodied humans have even greater reason to do so.
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r1.anchor: لما رغب الله رسوله في الذكر وفي المواظبة عليه ذكر عقيبه ما يقوي دواعيه في ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r2.speaker: المشبهة
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r2.claim: The anthropomorphists take “those who are with your Lord” to imply that God occupies a place and direction; Rāzī rejects this as impossible on the rational and transmitted proofs given under 7:54 and 10:3.
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r2.anchor: المشبهة تمسكوا بقوله : { إن الذين عند ربك } وقالوا لفظ { عند } مشعر بالمكان والجهة

RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r3.claim: The phrase can mean divine favor and mercy rather than location, as in the divine report that God is with hearts broken for His sake; this “withness” is not spatial.
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r3.anchor: هذه المعية بالفضل والرحمة لا بالجهة

RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r4.claim: “With your Lord” may mean nearness in honor: a minister is closer in rank to a ruler than a doorkeeper, even when the doorkeeper is physically nearer.
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r4.anchor: إن المراد القرب بالشرف . يقال : للوزير قربة عظيمة من الأمير

RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r5.claim: The wording also honors the angels by associating them with the honored abode where God placed them, the realm of lights, spirits, obedience, and blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v15p89#2/r5.anchor: هذا تشريف للملائكة بإضافتهم إلى الله من حيث إنه أسكنهم في المكان الذي كرمه وشرفه

RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r1.claim: A further sense is that the angels are God’s messengers to creation, like a caliph’s army said to be “with” him although its members are spread across the land.
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r1.anchor: لأنهم رسل الله إلى الخلق كما يقال : إن عند الخليفة جيشا عظيما

RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r2.claim: Abū Bakr al-Aṣamm uses the verse to argue that angels are superior to human beings: the Messenger is urged to worship by reference to the angels’ worship, which he says works only if they are superior.
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r2.anchor: تمسك أبو بكر الأصم رحمه الله بهذه الآية في إثبات أن الملائكة أفضل من البشر

RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r3.claim: The order puts glorification first because it is the heart’s knowledge and purification of God, then prostration as bodily action; this shows bodily worship branches from the heart’s acts.
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r3.anchor: وهذا الترتيب يدل على أن الأصل في الطاعة والعبودية أعمال القلوب

RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r4.claim: The phrase restricts the angels’ prostration to God, raising an apparent conflict with their prostration to Adam; Rāzī cites al-Ghazālī’s view that only earthly angels prostrated, not the great heavenly angels.
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ الغزالي : الذين سجدوا لآدم ملائكة الأرض . فأما عظماء ملائكة السموات فلا

RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r5.claim: Another reconciliation is that the verse’s statement is general while the command to prostrate to Adam is particular, and the particular takes precedence over the general.
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r5.anchor: وقيل أيضا : إن قوله : { وله يسجدون } يفيدون أنهم ما سجدوا لغير الله ، فهذا يفيد العموم

RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r6.claim: Rāzī links the verse to other descriptions of angels continually standing in worship and surrounding the Throne while praising God.
RAZI-FULL:v15p90/r6.anchor: وإنا لنحن الصافون * وإنا لنحن المسبحون

DURR-FULL:v3p639/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas lists prostrations in al-Aʿraf, al-Raʿd, al-Nahl, Bani Israʾil, Maryam, one in al-Hajj, al-Naml, al-Furqan, al-Sajdah, and Ha Mim al-Sajdah; no Mufassal prostration.
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه ذكر سجود القرآن فقال: الأعراف والرعد والنحل وبنو إسرائيل

DURR-FULL:v3p639/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r6.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r6.claim: Ata reports Ali ibn Abbas counted ten prostrations: al-Aʿraf, al-Raʿd, al-Nahl, Bani Israʾil, Maryam, first in al-Hajj, al-Furqan, al-Naml, al-Sajdah, and Ha Mim al-Sajdah.
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r6.anchor: عن عطاء قال: عد علي بن العباس عشر سجدات في القرآن

DURR-FULL:v3p639/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r7.claim: Abu al-Darda says he prostrated with the Prophet at eleven places, none in the Mufassal, including al-Aʿraf, al-Raʿd, al-Nahl, Bani Israʾil, Maryam, al-Hajj, al-Furqan, al-Naml, al-Sajdah, Sad, and a Hawamim prostration.
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r7.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال سجدت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إحدى عشرة سجدة

DURR-FULL:v3p639/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r8.claim: Amr ibn al-As reports the Prophet taught him fifteen prostrations in the Qur’an, three in the Mufassal and two in al-Hajj.
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r8.anchor: عن عمرو بن العاص أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أقرأه خمس عشرة سجدة في القرآن

DURR-FULL:v3p639/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r9.claim: Ibn Amr says the Prophet prostrated when reciting a sura containing prostration and the Companions followed, sometimes with no room for their foreheads.
DURR-FULL:v3p639/r9.anchor: عن ابن عمرو قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ علينا القرآن
